differences.detail: Model-family dispatch is hard-coded to OPT/Llama/Mistral/Qwen2/InternLM2 and raises ValueError for qwen3; the RoPE function name used by the R3 monkeypatch is only set for Llama/Mistral/Qwen2. Qwen3 must be dispatched (or the pipeline must find layers, norms, attention and apply_rotary_pos_emb from the model itself).

Norm fusion, RMSN replacement, QuantRMSNorm wrapping and stats hooks select norms by class. Qwen3RMSNorm is also the class of the per-head q_norm/k_norm, so class-based selection would replace them with RMSN(4096) (broadcast error, learned gamma lost) and attach A4 quantizers to pre-RoPE q/k. Select residual norms by name (input_layernorm, post_attention_layernorm, model.norm); leave q_norm/k_norm untouched, unquantized and frozen in block-AP (their weight would otherwise match the trainable-weight selector).
evidence: method.md Invariants (only residual-stream norms may be fused)

differences.detail: transformers 4.51 decoder layers take position_embeddings=(cos, sin) from model.model.rotary_emb instead of computing RoPE from position_ids, and the cache kwarg/return conventions differ from 4.40. The block-AP Catcher must capture position_embeddings (positions [P, P+L)) and every block call (update_dataset, train/eval, mse_init, block_mse_init_*, k_cache_mse_init) must pass it; check the layer return type instead of blindly taking [0].

The repo stores and feeds the prefix as a 4.40 legacy tuple (from_legacy_cache, kv_cache_repeat, tuple past_key_values in test_ppl, torch.save of output.past_key_values without map_location). On 4.51 build a fresh DynamicCache per forward from saved per-layer (K, V) fp16 tensors, batch-expanded, never reusing a mutated cache; save plain tensors and load with map_location. Masks must cover the P prefix columns (bottom-right causal; q_len != kv_len).

Prefix-token selection keys off model_name.split('-')[0] (qwen3 -> NotImplementedError) and picks eos_token as start token when the name contains 'qwen'. Qwen3 has no bos_token; for Qwen3-8B eos_token is <|im_end|>. Choose the start token generically (bos if defined, else the tokenizer's document-start/pad <|endoftext|>), log it, and handle zero detected outliers (assert outlier_num > 0) by falling back to the start token alone.

Reload (eval.py) re-wraps only RMSN/LlamaRMSNorm, so on Qwen3 the norm output quantizers are silently dropped, and the repo has no generate() path. The inference adapter must rebuild exactly the saved quantizer set (residual norms, o_proj/down_proj inputs, v_proj output, K wrapper), register the R4 online Hadamard (K=12) and the R3 wrapper, and inject a fresh prefix cache into every forward and generate call (real tokens at positions >= P; strip prefix ids from generate output).
RMSN hard-codes eps 1e-5; Qwen3 rms_norm_eps is 1e-6. Use config.rms_norm_eps at quantize time and reload.
head_dim is computed as hidden_size/num_attention_heads. Equal to config.head_dim (128) for Qwen3-8B, but wrong for other Qwen3 sizes; read config.head_dim.
block_mse_init_static's fine pass calls the block without attention_mask (repo bug); with a prefix this changes the masking. Pass the same mask/position_embeddings as the coarse pass.
intermediate_size 12288 = 12 x 1024, which get_hadK supports (K=12), so R4 applies as written.
Qwen3 has no linear biases and untied embeddings, so the bias-rotation and tied-embedding paths are unused.

R3 Hadamard and K quantization sit in the apply_rotary_pos_emb wrapper, i.e. after q_norm/k_norm and RoPE and before the cache write, which is the right place. Never use --k_pre_rope (would quantize before k_norm/RoPE) and never fold R3 into weights.
GQA 32/8 is already handled: rotate_ov_proj reshapes by KV heads, k_cache_mse_init uses repeat_kv, K/V scales are [8, 1].

No released W4A4 kernel: int_linear_real is weight-only GPTQ-style packing with dequant+fp16 matmul. The artifact is fake-quant fp16 weights plus scales, so no VRAM/speed win without a later kernel stage, and vLLM export is activation_bits_unsupported.
Q is never quantized; the R3 Hadamard on q is applied after q_norm and RoPE inside the RoPE wrapper, so q_norm only changes what precedes R3, not the invariant (same Hadamard on q and k after RoPE).

Qwen3-8B layer 16 (only that layer) has token-wise outliers in the down_proj input (after the R4 Hadamard) triggered by the content token "2" (id 17) at arbitrary positions: per-token max top-1/median up to 2166 over 32 Pile samples. Prefixing only absorbs outliers at fixed initial/delimiter positions, so it cannot remove a content-triggered one, and the O2 per-tensor static A4 scale cannot cover both the outlier token and the bulk: block 16 mlp.down_proj_input_quantizer MSE-init best_loss 9.51 (block 15: 0.0015) at clip factor 1.0, block val loss 0.108 -> 28-32 for the rest of block-AP. Use PrefixQuant-O1 (paper Table 1: per-channel W4, per-token dynamic A4, group-wise 128 dynamic KV4) with the learnable per-layer activation clipping (--activation_clipping), keeping the prefix tokens, rotations, mse_init and block-AP. The artifact then carries clipping factors (bound_factor) instead of activation/KV scales; reload must rebuild dynamic quantizers and load them.
